一時之間，翻蓋式還是摺疊式才是摺疊智能手機的未來並不明朗，但至少目前看來，書本式摺疊機顯然是贏家。

Samsung's eighth-generation foldable phone adopts this design, the anticipated iPhone Ultra is expected to do the same, and leaked images of the Xiaomi 18 Fold follow the same trend...

There are two form factors for foldable smartphones, commonly known as flip-style and fold-style.

A flip-style design essentially folds a traditional smartphone in half, resulting in a thicker device with half the height, offering a standard-sized screen in a more pocketable form factor. The Motorola Razr is one such example, with a design lineage tracing back to the company's first popular model in 2004.

The fold-style design is increasingly being referred to as the 'book-style' design for obvious reasons—it unfolds a more square-ish device into a small tablet like the iPad mini. This is the design Apple is expected to unveil next month.

Samsung popularized this design with its Galaxy Z Fold series, with the eighth-generation model having just been unveiled at the end of last month.

Xiaomi is now preparing to join the fray with the 18 Fold, whose camera module design shares quite a few similarities with the anticipated iPhone Ultra. Weibo user Peter shared two images (above), suspecting they are engineering prototypes rather than actual production units.

Our sister site 9to5Google pointed out that the deep cherry color appears to be inspired by one of the rumored color options for the iPhone 18 Pro.
